name: Alexander Lukashenka
summary: Lukashenka has preserved state ownership in major sectors and used presidential powers to steer investment and regulate prices. He has concentrated political authority in the presidency and suppressed organized opposition. His foreign policy has increasingly tied Belarus to Russia through economic integration and military cooperation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The constitution Lukashenka put to referendum guarantees citizens free treatment in state health institutions.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lukashenka assigns priority sectors for investment and preserves state direction and preferential financing for major enterprises.

public-ownership.rationale: His government kept major industrial enterprises under state ownership and confined privatization largely to loss-making firms in which the state had only a minority interest.

property-fundamental.rationale: His constitutional changes retained judicial and compensation requirements for compulsory acquisition. His government subsequently obtained legal authority to seize assets linked to states it designated unfriendly.

strong-leader.rationale: Lukashenka used the 1996 referendum to give the presidency far greater authority, including the power to issue decrees with the force of law.

state-harmful.rationale: Lukashenka’s constitutional changes expanded the state presidency and established a new national body to set strategic policy.

traditional-family.rationale: In his UN address he described the family as a basic foundation of society and identified strengthening it as a continuing priority of his government.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The constitutional amendment he put to referendum defines marriage as the union of a woman and a man.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His constitutional revision assigns the state responsibility for preserving Belarus’s historical, cultural and spiritual heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: He described his preferred approach to institutional reform as evolutionary, preserving traditions and developing existing structures.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He issued the decree making Belarus a party to the Paris Agreement and committed the country to a national emissions reduction target.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He issued the decree authorizing construction of the Belarusian nuclear power plant at Astravets.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: He defended evolutionary political development and described the attempted color revolution in Belarus as an illegitimate bid to overturn the country’s institutions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Lukashenka and the Council of Ministers designate priority sectors for investment, including machinery, transport infrastructure and information technology.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The constitution retains the National Bank and gives it exclusive legal authority over currency issuance.

democracy-best.rationale: Lukashenka consolidated power through the 1996 referendum, and his administration restricted genuine opposition competition and refused transparent election oversight in 2020.

direct-votes.rationale: Lukashenka repeatedly put major constitutional changes, including presidential powers and eligibility, to nationwide referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: His constitutional restructuring retained a national parliament and created an assembly made up of state officials, local deputies and civil society representatives.

separate-church-state.rationale: He signed a religion law giving the state extensive oversight of religious associations and recognizing the historical role of particular denominations.

private-courts-defense.rationale: His constitutional model assigns justice to state courts and provides for a Supreme Court heading the ordinary judiciary.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He described Belarusians as a national community encompassing more than 150 ethnic groups and nationalities.

civilizational-union.rationale: He signed the treaty creating a political Union State with Russia, grounded in the historical and spiritual ties of the two peoples and common institutions.

limit-population.rationale: His family capital decree provides a state payment specifically to encourage families to have a third or subsequent child.

conscription.rationale: His constitution makes defence a civic obligation and provides for statutory military service and its alternatives.

territorial-expansion.rationale: In his 2024 Assembly address he rejected seeking any other country’s land and said Belarus should defend and live on its existing territory.

class-collaboration.rationale: Article 14 of the constitution he retained makes cooperation among government, employers’ associations and trade unions the basis of labour relations.

dominated-front.rationale: He urged CIS states to confront Western pressure collectively and to coordinate with organisations such as BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The government failed to bring security personnel to account for documented abuses after the 2020 election, including beatings and torture in detention.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He used state power to extend family allowances and direct strategic industrial investment.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: His government enacted stricter rules on political associations, and his constitutional revision prohibits associations aiming to change the constitutional order by force.

separated-powers.rationale: He overrode the Constitutional Court’s ruling on the 1996 referendum and used the outcome to expand presidential decree and appointment powers.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: His government maintained substantial legal limits on exercising the right to strike, and authorities detained and prosecuted strike organisers after the 2020 election.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He presented the coexistence of many ethnic groups in Belarus as compatible with national harmony and used mixed families as an example.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution he put to referendum permits temporary restrictions on rights and freedoms during a state of emergency or martial law, but places specified rights beyond suspension.

party-controls-media.rationale: He replaced editors at leading newspapers after taking power, and later enacted amendments further expanding state control over the media.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He signed the Union State treaty delegating specified legislative and policy powers to common Union institutions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The constitution under Lukashenka puts the armed forces under the president as commander-in-chief and gives him appointment and dismissal power over the senior command.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: His 2004 referendum abolished presidential term limits. His 2022 revision restored a two-term limit effective when the next presidential term began.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His Union State treaty commits Belarus to a common defence policy and military cooperation with Russia.

death-penalty.rationale: He signed legislation widening capital punishment to certain acts of treason by officials and military personnel.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Lukashenka retained direct presidential elections through his constitutional revisions, including the provision for a second popular ballot when required.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Lukashenka appoints the central bank’s board and approves its reports, and his government has intervened in monetary and exchange-rate policy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: His constitutional revision retained the provision that exercising property rights must not run counter to public benefit or safety or harm the environment.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The religion law he signed requires religious organizations to register again and exposes them to state dissolution for specified violations.

common-currency.rationale: The Union State treaty he signed establishes the goal of a common currency and a single issuing centre for the union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Lukashenka signed a treaty creating common political institutions with Russia on the basis of the historical and cultural kinship of the two peoples.

ban-cartels.rationale: The antimonopoly decree establishes enforcement powers, but the material reviewed did not settle a categorical prohibition on cartels.

public-money-creation.rationale: The constitution reserves the issuance of money exclusively to the National Bank, a state institution.

elective-rulers.rationale: The constitutional model Lukashenka put to referendum selects the president through a popular presidential election.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1996 changes made presidential decrees a source of binding law, and the government subsequently treated presidential decrees as superior to ordinary legislation.

filial-duty.rationale: The constitution he put to referendum obliges children to care for and assist their parents.

single-official-language.rationale: The constitution Lukashenka put to referendum in 2022 retained equal official status for Belarusian and Russian.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: He signed a decree restricting uses of foreign gratuitous aid and requiring its registration.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He extended the family capital programme with a lump-sum account for families upon the birth or adoption of a third or subsequent child.

religious-nation.rationale: He defined Belarusian national unity in terms that encompass many ethnic groups and the adherents of several major religions, whose religious centres he treated as shared national symbols.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His government detained opposition figures and protesters in 2020. In 2023 he enacted a law raising party membership thresholds fivefold and requiring existing parties to register again.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His constitutional changes retain the armed forces and assign their command and senior appointments to the president.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Lukashenka bound Belarus to military cooperation with Russia and subsequently authorized Russian forces to use Belarusian territory for the attack on Ukraine.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He set aside a Constitutional Court ruling on the binding effect of the 1996 referendum and subsequently used decree powers to govern without ordinary legislation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution Lukashenka put to referendum specifies that spouses have equal rights in marriage and family life.

abolish-ip.rationale: The constitution he retained through his 2022 revision expressly protects intellectual property.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Lukashenka agreed to the stationing of Russian nuclear weapons in Belarus after securing the removal of the constitutional aspiration to nuclear-free status.

recognise-genocide.rationale: He signed the law formally recognizing the wartime mass killings of the Belarusian people as genocide.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: His constitutional revision obliges the state to preserve the memory of the Belarusian people’s wartime sacrifices and accomplishments.

independent-unions.rationale: His government dissolved the principal independent trade unions in 2022 and prosecuted their leaders, while giving the official trade union federation a privileged role.

second-chamber.rationale: His 1996 restructuring replaced the single Supreme Soviet with a bicameral National Assembly, and the 2022 constitution retains both chambers.

family-wage.rationale: Article 42 of the constitution he retained sets a wage floor intended to ensure workers and their families a dignified living.

future-generations.rationale: At COP28 he argued that consuming natural resources to accumulate private wealth deprives future generations and called for protecting their ability to live on Earth.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He argued that changes to Belarus’s institutions should preserve the existing order and develop structures inherited from the Soviet period.

public-service-media.rationale: He appointed replacement editors at leading newspapers and signed a law authorizing the Information Ministry to ban media outlets in specified circumstances.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: His government cut internet access around the 2020 presidential election and protests, then amended telecommunications law to authorize shutdowns on national security grounds.

equal-conscription.rationale: No recorded position found that settles equal draft obligations.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: No recorded position found that settles the organisation of politics along denominational lines.

national-resource-control.rationale: The constitution Lukashenka retained reserves subsoil, waters and forests to state ownership, and he directed the development of the Petrikov potash deposit by Belaruskali.

multipolar-world.rationale: He called for a global order with several centres of power and argued that the West might continue as one centre within it.

no-central-bank.rationale: His constitutional model retains the National Bank and makes it the central bank of Belarus.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: He enacted financial support for larger families and made support for family upbringing a constitutional priority.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: During the October 2022 surge in prices he imposed an immediate ban on price increases.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: In the published portion of his 2025 address he pointed to the recurring National Festival of Cultures as part of Belarus’s policy of fostering national cohesion across ethnic groups.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: His 2022 surveillance decree obliges telecom operators and internet service and resource providers to give security services access to user data on request.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: The constitution under Lukashenka empowers the president to dissolve the parliamentary chambers under specified conditions.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: His 2015 decree levied a special charge on working-age residents who had worked fewer than 183 days the preceding year, subject to exemptions. This used a financial penalty to encourage work.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The constitution he put to referendum prohibits torture as well as cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

criminalize-genocide-denial.rationale: The 2022 genocide law introduced criminal liability for public denial of the genocide of the Belarusian people.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: He presented the new powers of the People’s Assembly as a development of existing Belarusian and Soviet institutions.

notes: Research covered constitutional and election history, political methods, civil liberties, labour and economic policy, families, religion, language and heritage, alliances and international institutions, the environment, and technology. The UN General Debate corpus identified the 2015 speech, checked against the UN verbatim record. Project Gutenberg returned no matching author. The 2022 constitutional revision restored a prospective two-term limit after the 2004 removal. The audit uses the official health entitlement as evidence for universal public provision to citizens. Other entries are null where the record located did not settle the full proposition.
